name: Roland RD-88
description: Roland RD-88 stage piano: the temporary scene (common, the Tone, EQ, MFX and Zone blocks of each of its three zones, the IFX, chorus, reverb and sympathetic resonance), the setup, and the system blocks (common, controllers, system chorus and reverb, master EQ and comp, input reverb and EQ), from the MIDI Implementation.

sources.title: RD-88 MIDI Implementation (version 1.12, Jul. 22, 2020)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from RD-88_MIDI_Imple_eng03_W.pdf (sha256 c6fecbbb109a1436ab27b1a5afc877dd8b71b6fb522f291084c34c5bb873efa2). Model ID 00 00 00 64, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

The three zones are the map's Scene Tone(n), Scene EQ(n), Scene MFX(n) and Scene Zone(n), n = 1-3, laid out as zone<n>.tone, zone<n>.eq, zone<n>.mfx and zone<n>. The map does not name them; the Sympathetic Resonance block's SymReso Part row lists OFF, UPPER1, UPPER2, LOWER (p18), and Scene Common's Voice Reserve rows are numbered Layer(1)-(3).

Scene MFX(n) are laid at 01 00 30 00, 01 00 32 00 and 01 00 34 00, two address pages apart: the MFX block is 00 00 01 10 (144 bytes) and crosses into the next page. The Scene IFX at 01 00 50 00 is the same table.

Setup (02 00 00 00) holds which scene is current, as a bank select and program change (Scene BS MSB, Scene BS LSB, Scene PC); it is marked system with the System blocks, so the startup read leaves it and them alone.

Sympathetic Resonance 00 0B, "Rev HF Damp" (p18), is printed with a bit layout (00aa aaaa) and a label list but no range. The reader counts its 32 labels (16 Hz … 15000 Hz, Bypass) and lays it as 0 - 31. The row with the very same labels and bit layout, AtkIn LPF at 00 03, is printed (1 - 32), so the real wire values may be 1 - 32 and every label here one value low; unverified until an instrument answers. Its counterpart Rev LF Damp (00 0C, "Bypass, 16 … 15000") is printed (0 - 31), like AtkIn HPF.
No noPull: a zone always plays one tone through the same Scene Tone, EQ, MFX and Zone blocks, and the map has no alternative tone areas that the instrument might not answer for.

Identity (p12 in each manual): the RD-88, the RD-88EX and the RD-08 all print family code 64 03 and family number code 00 00, the status line and the byte table agreeing. The RD-88 and RD-88EX print the same software revision as well (00 01 00 01), so nothing in their replies tells them apart; the RD-08 differs only in its revision bytes (01 01 00 00), which profiles do not pin (a firmware update is not a different instrument). The three therefore collide: choosing any of these profiles for one of the others is not flagged as a mismatch. They share one address map, so the profiles agree wherever they overlap.
Bank Select (p1): the Scene table's last row, LSB 003 programs 001-016, is numbered "384 - 400"; sixteen programs after scene 384 are 385-400, as laid out.

Bank Select (p1), the Tone table: the second PCM group is printed "RR-B" (for PR-B) and its LSB 065 row "0128 - 0256" (for 0129 - 0256). Tones are chosen per zone in its Scene Tone block (bank select MSB/LSB and program change), which the scene presets do not list.
The worked example (p23) is headed "Setting program level to 74"; its text and address are Scene Common's Scene Level (01 00 00 10), and its bytes are checked as printed.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the instrument receives and transmits as Control Change (received p1-4, transmitted p8-11) is not mapped yet
coverage.zones: all three zones' Scene Tone, Scene EQ, MFX and Scene Zone blocks (01 00 10 00-12 00, 01 00 20 00-22 00, 01 00 30 00/32 00/34 00, 01 00 40 00-42 00)
coverage.tones: none in the map: a zone's tone is chosen by bank and program (Scene Tone 00 00-00 02) from the tone list in the Bank Select table (p1), and the address map has no tone, piano-designer or tone-modify area. What a scene can change of its zones' tones is the Scene Tone block's part offsets and the zone's EQ and MFX, all laid out
coverage.userScenes: not edit buffer: User Scene(001)-(400) at 10 00 00 00 + (n-1) x 00 01 00 00, to 13 0F 00 00 (p12), each the Scene layout again
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX, IFX, chorus and reverb parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list. MFX Type (0-90), Chorus Type (0-9) and Reverb Type (0-7) print no labels
